items.title: Peel Region Begins Sewer Rehab on Ponytrail Drive, Expects Lane Reductions Into November
items.summary: Peel Region says crews have begun rehabilitating the sanitary sewer along Ponytrail Drive, a busy neighbourhood road in Mississauga's east end that runs between Bloor Street and Burnhamthorpe Road East. According to the region, the work started this week and is expected to continue into November, though the timeline could shift because of weather or other unexpected issues. Officials explained in a notice to nearby residents and businesses that sanitary sewers carry wastewater from homes to a water resource recovery facility, and crews will clean the pipe before lining it with a new resin coating to extend its lifespan. The region said Capital Sewer Services Inc. is carrying out the work under contract, generally during weekday daytime hours. Project leaders noted traffic on the street may be temporarily reduced to a single lane while the work is underway, and signage will be posted to direct drivers when that happens.

items.title: Mississauga Bowling Alley Owner Turns Lanes Into Concert Stage to Honour Nephew's Memory
items.summary: Insauga.com reports that Ed Sousa, a director at Mississauga's Classic Bowl, has transformed the bowling centre into an unexpected concert venue, drawing established Canadian and international acts without requiring fans to travel into downtown Toronto. According to the outlet, the next show lands Sunday, Oct. 25, when Saga frontman Michael Sadler performs at the venue alongside guest David Barrett. The outlet reports Sousa's concert programming has grown into three series: McBowl, an annual charity music festival; Rock and Bowl, which features intimate performances; and Pop Up Shows, booked around touring artists passing through the region. Sousa told insauga.com the effort traces back to a personal loss, after his nephew was diagnosed with leukemia in 1987 and died at 17 on Halloween night in 1992, years during which his sister stayed on and off at Ronald McDonald House Charities Canada. According to the outlet, Sousa said he doesn't know how families with sick children get by without that support, which is why the shows keep raising money for the charity.

items.title: Frost Advisory Returns for Second Straight Night Across Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory covering Mississauga and Brampton for the second consecutive night, according to insauga.com, with the warning also extending to St. Catharines, Grimsby, Niagara Falls, Welland and the broader Niagara Region. The agency said patchy frost is expected overnight, mainly away from the lakes, with forecasters predicting temperatures could dip to around 2 C. Environment Canada advised residents to take preventative measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees and crops before temperatures drop. The outlet reports this is the latest in a string of frost advisories Environment Canada has issued across the region this week, following a similar alert that covered both cities the previous night. Officials noted conditions can vary by location, with inland areas typically seeing the most significant frost.

items.title: Garnetwood Park Upgrade Moves Past Concrete Forming Phase as Mississauga Adds New Amenities
items.summary: Insauga.com reports construction is underway on a major upgrade to Garnetwood Park, a 34-acre green space in Mississauga's east end near Burnhamthorpe Road East and Ponytrail Drive. According to Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca, crews have finished the concrete forming phase, where formwork molds were built ahead of pouring concrete, and are now moving into the next stage of construction. The outlet reports the park already includes basketball nets, a leash-free zone, a mobile food vendor, a multi-use court, a playground, a soccer field, a softball diamond and a renovated spray pad, along with a four-court tennis facility that opened last year through a partnership between the city, Tennis Canada and National Bank. Fonseca said the city is responding to community feedback by adding two new paved trail paths, four-season seating and tables, a seasonal ice rink surface and pickleball courts. Neither Fonseca nor city officials have given a specific completion date for the remaining amenities, the outlet reports.

items.title: Hurontario Street Closure Near Burnhamthorpe Signals Ramp-Up in Hazel McCallion LRT Work
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a major Mississauga intersection partially closed Thursday night as part of expanding construction on the $6-billion Hazel McCallion Line, with the closure expected to last until early Monday morning, Oct. 26. According to the outlet, MiWay, the city's transit provider, has detoured several bus routes until the closure lifts. The outlet reports Metrolinx, the provincial agency overseeing what it calls the largest transit project in Mississauga's history, says construction activity will intensify along Hurontario Street between Burnhamthorpe Road and Eglinton Avenue through the end of December. Metrolinx said in an online update that current work includes track installation and maintenance, electrical and telecommunications work, landscaping, roadwork and the installation of shelters at surface-level LRT stops. According to insauga.com, drivers should expect additional temporary road closures over the next couple of months and potentially beyond as the work continues.

items.title: City of Mississauga Urges Residents to Winterize Homes Before Cold Weather Sets In
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is encouraging homeowners to inspect and prepare their properties now, before colder temperatures arrive, to help prevent costly winter damage. According to the city, this seasonal upkeep guards against fire risk from heating sources, water damage from frozen pipes, and structural damage caused by wind, ice and heavy snow. The city recommends clearing eavestroughs and downspouts of leaves and debris to maintain proper drainage, and suggests disconnecting roof downspouts from pipes tied to basement weepers, directing runoff onto lawns instead using an elbow extension that keeps water at least three feet from the foundation. Officials also advise pruning trees and hedges before winter arrives, saying it supports healthy spring growth and reduces the risk of damage from heavy snowfall. The city further recommends storing rain barrels and shutting off outdoor faucets to conserve water, prevent flooding and protect plumbing from freezing over the colder months.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Volunteer Applications to Keep Natural Ice Rinks Running This Winter
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is accepting volunteer applications for its natural ice rink program, which gives residents free outdoor spots to skate and play hockey each winter, according to mississauga.com. The outlet reports the program is entirely volunteer-run, and the city says 102 people took part last winter to help maintain local rinks across the municipality. According to the city, applications are open until Nov. 15, and managing a single rink requires a minimum of three volunteers to handle daily upkeep. The outlet reports the natural ice rink season is weather-dependent but is expected to begin in mid-December and run through March 2027. Volunteers interested in getting involved are asked to apply directly through the city's website before the deadline, officials said.

items.title: Tedjo Emerges as Possible Third Contender as Parrish-Crombie Feud Turns Personal
items.summary: The National Observer reports what was expected to be a two-way showdown between incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie has grown contentious enough that some voters are now eyeing a third option. According to the outlet, a heated debate saw both candidates trade barbs, with Crombie telling Canada's National Observer that Parrish can be very Trumpian, while saying she herself never resorted to name-calling even though she pushed back on Parrish's comments. The outlet reports Parrish countered that the debate's moderator should have stepped in sooner to stop candidates from speaking out of turn, acknowledging afterward that she probably lost her cool a bit while insisting no one behaved particularly well. According to political scientist Randy Besco of the University of Toronto, Councillor Alvin Tedjo could emerge as a serious challenger, pointing to his close polling numbers and a first-ever endorsement from the Peel Regional Police Association. The outlet reports this marks Tedjo's second mayoral run after losing to Parrish in 2024, following an earlier bid for the Ontario Liberal Party leadership in 2020.

items.title: She Carries the Song Tour Brings Three Indigenous Singer-Songwriters to Mississauga's Living Arts Centre
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports three Indigenous singers and songwriters are touring regional venues across Ontario, including a stop at the Living Arts Centre in Mississauga, as part of a show called She Carries the Song. According to the outlet, the lineup features Abenaki (W8banaki) artist Mimi O'Bonsawin, Cree artist Celeigh Cardinal and Oneida/Mohawk artist Lacey Hill, performing together at the venue on Living Arts Drive. The outlet reports the tour began in Ottawa and will continue through Guelph, Oakville and Toronto, coordinated by Ontario Presents along with booking agencies and local performing arts centres. O'Bonsawin told Mississauga News the performance blends music with storytelling, as each artist shares personal history, cultural roots and the inspiration behind her songs. According to the outlet, O'Bonsawin, who released a new record in August, said the format lets audiences experience three distinct musical styles across a single evening.

items.title: Eglinton Avenue Closes at Hurontario Through the Weekend for Hazel McCallion LRT Work
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports a portion of Eglinton Avenue at Hurontario Street closed temporarily from Thursday, Oct. 22 through Monday, Oct. 26 to allow construction on the Hazel McCallion Line. According to a Metrolinx news release cited by the outlet, drivers using Eglinton Avenue during the closure will need to detour using McLaughlin Road, Bristol Road and Kennedy Road to the north, or Sorrento Drive and Elia Avenue to the south. The outlet reports Hurontario Street itself will remain open with one lane running in each direction throughout the closure. According to mississauga.com, MiWay will also detour several bus routes during the work, including routes 35 and 135 in both directions and routes 17 and 103 in both directions. The outlet reports a map of the affected detours is available through the transit agency.
